en.title: The Sun That Dwells Within Us
en.excerpt: December in a foreign winter brings a sweet longing for home — and an invitation to rediscover a warmth that is born of encounter and sharing.
en.content:
Text: Ana Luiza A Duarte

Integrative Therapist

December arrives like a warm embrace in the middle of the cold.

While the streets light up and the world seems to deck itself out in promises, there are those who feel

a sweet longing — for home, for family, for language, for the smell of fresh coffee coming from

the kitchen. It is the heart trying to find its place even far from the place of origin.

It is natural to miss the sun that kept us company all year round. To miss the light that warmed

our skin, the full table, the familiar voices. But perhaps it is now, in the middle of this foreign

winter, that we can rediscover another kind of warmth — the one born of

encounter, of sharing, of presence.

Longing can be a bridge. It can lead us to the other, to the new community that welcomes us, to the

affinities that bring us closer. An invitation to open the doors of the house and of the heart, to

create bonds that warm us when the sun takes its time to appear.

And, as the year says goodbye, something in us also reorganises itself. The silence between one

celebration and the next invites us to look inward: what do we want to carry forward? What

shall we let bloom again from 2025?

There is always a spark that resists, even on the shortest days.

Perhaps the secret is to remember that the light we seek so much on the outside also lives

within us.

That the warmth of the summer left behind can be rekindled in the smile of a new friend,

in a gesture of care, in a moment of gratitude.

So, this December, light your own sun.

Gather. Share. Celebrate — even from a distance.

Because, when we meet one another, home happens again — wherever we are.

Ana Luiza A Duarte

Integrative Therapist
en.meta_desc: December far from home: how longing can become a bridge, and why the light we search for outside also lives within us.

en.title: The Winter of the Ego — A Poetic Rebirth
en.excerpt: There is a winter inside every soul, where the Ego loosens its grip and everything that is excess begins to fall away.
en.content:
Text written by: Aria Milioni

Systemic Therapist

There is a season within every soul in which everything grows quieter.

A gentle inner Winter, where the Ego loosens its control and everything that is excess begins to fall away.

Winter is not punishment — it is preparation.

It strips us bare with lightness, like trees letting go of their leaves, to reveal what is

true beneath the noise: procrastination, fear, resistance, the unconscious search for

validation.

All that limits our capacity to give, to evolve and to serve.

This is the sacred process of deconstructing the Ego — the clearing of the inner soil.

When we surrender, even in silence, we send our intention out to the Universe.

Not from the need of the Ego to receive, but from the readiness of the soul to grow.

True spirituality begins here: in honesty, in service, in the willingness to let old identities dissolve.

Winter teaches us our limits and our desires, what no longer belongs, and what still

pulses to stay.

And then, without effort, Spring arrives.

Spring is born when the Ego softens, when the inner ground thaws enough for new seeds to take root.

Suddenly, clarity turns into action, love turns into presence and the act of giving becomes the natural language of the heart.

There is no flowering without its Winter.

You do not plant in frozen soil.

You must allow yourself to be taken apart first.

This is the rhythm of healing:

Winter cleanses.

Spring is reborn.

And the soul, patient and luminous, crosses the bridge between the two.

Text written by: Aria Milioni

Systemic Therapist
en.meta_desc: Winter as the sacred deconstruction of the Ego: how inner quiet, service and surrender prepare the ground for a poetic rebirth.

en.title: Sun and Moon: Balancing Awareness and Emotions Through the Northern European Winter
en.excerpt: The Sun and the Moon shape both our awareness and our emotions — and through the long northern winter, keeping them in balance takes small, steady choices.
en.content:
Text written by: Aria Milioni

Systemic Therapist

The Sun and the Moon play a fascinating role in our lives, influencing both our awareness and our emotions.

The Sun, with its majestic presence, is our central star, providing the vital energy that keeps us alive. It symbolises awareness, self-affirmation and the ability to express our own light in the world. When we think of the Sun, we can imagine the strength and confidence it inspires in us, like a powerful and just lion.

On the other hand, the Moon is the queen of emotions and of emotional intelligence. It reflects the light of the Sun and is intimately connected to our most sensitive side. The Moon not only influences the tides and nature, but also our feelings, intuitions and memories. Each lunar phase affects us in a unique way, from the introspection of the new moon to the intensity of the full moon.

During the winter in northern Europe, when the days are short and the nights long, keeping mental and emotional balance can be challenging. Here are a few practical tips to help you face this season:

  • Expose yourself to natural light whenever possible: Make the most of sunny moments to help regulate your biological clock and improve your mood.

  • Practise physical activity regularly: Exercise not only warms the body, but also releases endorphins, which are essential for mental wellbeing.

  • Keep a routine: Having fixed times to wake up, eat and sleep helps maintain emotional stability.

  • Cultivate moments of self-care: Meditation, relaxing reading or a warm bath can help calm the mind and nourish the emotions.

  • Connect with other people: Even if the weather invites isolation, keeping in touch with friends and family is crucial for emotional support.

It is interesting to note that various cultures around the world have different interpretations of the influence of the Sun and the Moon on our lives. While some see the Sun as a symbol of authority and leadership, others may associate it with a spiritual guide. In the same way, the Moon, in its constant change, is seen as a magical and seductive force that invites us to reflect and to connect with our inner self.

Would you like to know more about how these celestial forces can influence your day-to-day life? Leave your comment and I will bring more information in the next article

Aria Milioni

Systemic Therapist
en.meta_desc: How the Sun and Moon influence awareness and emotion, plus five practical ways to stay balanced through the dark northern European winter.
